H_hierarchical.evidence: The controller has a flat mode set: off, ready-to-run, grid-connected, islanded, and fault; the paper groups active states but does not define nested sub-states.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Mode choices depend on grid availability/operator-required islanding, BESS activation uses LV dc bus thresholds with an OR condition, and fault transitions depend on any system fault.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Transitions/modes include ordered startup of PCS/sources/BESS/loads, stopping PCS bus-voltage control on islanding, sending BESS voltage-control commands, droop-mode switching, setpoint issuing, protection updates, and data logging.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper states a global rule from every active state except off into fault, and fault recovery must go through ready-to-run after clearance.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Grid-connected/islanded behavior is introduced in the operation-modes section, transitions and BESS threshold behavior are in the state-machine section, and protection/fault handling appears in a separate protection section and test section.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as islanded mode, grid-forming/grid-following, load shedding, fault ride-through, protection coordination, and reconnection imply domain-specific transition and action semantics.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are not in a compact state/action table; PCS, BESS, source, load, relay, and logging behaviors are attributed from narrative prose around the mode descriptions.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: At least one mode condition combines grid unavailability with operator request, and BESS control is guarded by a low-threshold OR high-threshold LV dc bus condition.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No parent/composite state is defined with its own entry/during/exit behavior; the mode machine is essentially flat.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: All active modes share the same transition to fault, followed by the single recovery path fault to ready-to-run.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are boolean/comparison guard families around grid availability, operator-required islanding, BESS thresholds, and faults, but not enough explicit arithmetic guard sets for a strong SMT advantage.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The global any-active-state fault transition applies to at least ready-to-run, grid-connected, and islanded, so forced transitions avoid duplicating the same escape edge.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Some side effects are abstract controller outputs such as dispatch commands, protection-setting updates, and data logging, while core mode actions are still concrete PCS/BESS commands.

key_nl_quotes: All the active states ... can go to the fault state
below a threshold value Vth1 or higher than ... Vth2
one_line_pitch: A flat but action-heavy F-CHP mode manager with thresholded BESS handover, prose-scattered mode semantics, and a global fault escape rule that weak baselines must duplicate correctly.
rationale: This is a strong stress-test for actions, guards, and global recovery rather than hierarchy. The paper gives enough concrete behavior to build a reference EFSM: startup sequencing, grid-connected/islanded handover, BESS threshold control, reconnection, and mandatory restart after faults. Its main baseline trap is that the semantics are split across operation-mode, state-machine, protection, and testing prose, while the global fault transition must be applied consistently across all active modes.
